decision.title: Node items, accessors and JNodes (packet )
decision.summary: Node items are inline and retain their tree; string value, typed value and base URI follow the listed rules; a JNode cell holds parent, key, value and child position, compared by position paths.

item.p: Node items are inline ( layout) and retain their tree.
String value of a document or element walks the index range up to () for text nodes; one text node is passed as is, more are joined in heap scratch memory released before returning.

Typed value: derived (xs:untypedAtomic for documents, text, elements, attributes; xs:string for comments, PIs, namespace nodes) when the annotation is none, xs:untyped or xs:untypedAtomic, or the tree has no get_typed_value; otherwise the tree answers.

Base URI: the xml:base values of the element and its ancestors, up to the first absolute one, resolved outermost-in against the tree's base URI (RFC 3986, section 5.2.2, strict; checked on all 42 examples of section 5.4). A relative value with no base is kept as written. No base URI for namespace nodes and for parentless attributes, text and comments; a parentless PI has the tree's. xml:base values are not percent-encoded first (XML Base, section 3.1).

JNodes: one cell holds parent (retained), key, value, child position, child count (computed at make), depth and JTree identifier (issued last, so a failed root uses none). Under a map: one child per entry; an array: per member; two or more items: per item, keyed by position from 1; anything else is a leaf. Identity and order compare the paths of child positions from the root in O(depth) without memory: equal positions under one parent select the same key, so this is XDM's "same parent and atomic-equal key". The generic node functions live in src/xdm_json_node.c.
